Applies to this chat only. Appended in list order — earlier means more weight.
A preset is a named block of prompt text. Write one, then come back and switch it on.

Presets are pluggable prompt modules. This page only creates and edits them. Which ones are active is chosen per conversation under "⋯ → Presets" at the top right of the chat — what you turn on in one topic never leaks into another.
Save prompts you use often — a code reviewer, a fiction partner — and switch them on when needed.
Pick a file to use as a preset: plain text, Markdown, JSON, YAML and docx all work. You can still edit it afterwards.
Text cannot be extracted from a PDF (Android\'s built-in PDF library can only render it). Copy the content into a text file first.

Every file change made after this reply is undone: files it created are deleted, files it edited are restored. The conversation also steps back to this point. The old branch is kept — switch versions to get it back.
No file changes after this message — only the conversation will be truncated.

Cannot read this folder — enable all-files access in Permissions
For a container workspace, enter the host path of that folder inside the Ubuntu rootfs, e.g. /storage/emulated/0/ubuntu/rootfs/home/user/app. Reads, writes and commands act on it directly.
These are the system capabilities the app uses. Each takes effect only after you grant it, and can be revoked at any time.
No direct entry found — open App info and look for it there
Accessibility and all-files access are system switches. Only you can turn them on in system settings — no app can do it for you.
Tell you when a long task finishes in the background.
Without it: keep the app open to see results.
Bind the workspace to a real folder on storage.
Without it: only the internal workspace works.
Show a small banner while the agent controls the screen.
Without it: actions still work, but you cannot see what it touches.
Read the current screen\'s controls and tap, type or swipe.
Without it: the whole screen-control toolset is unavailable.
Keep long tasks alive in the background.
Without it: long tasks may be killed when the screen locks.
Once enabled, the agent can read the current screen and act on it with your consent — tap buttons, fill forms, scroll lists, go back.
This is an accessibility service. It only looks at the foreground screen, never at apps in the background.
Foreground only: no background apps, no notification contents.
Password fields are never read or tapped; screens containing them are never captured.
Every action must carry a fresh snapshot; if the screen changed, it refuses.
Stoppable at any time: flip the system switch off and it is gone.
Screen control is off by default. While it is on, every tap shows up as a tool card in the conversation.
Allow DSHA to read the current screen and tap or type on it. Active only while you keep it enabled.
Let the agent control this phone\'s screen
Put the workspace on a public machine — nothing on this phone.

The workspace lives on a remote machine; the phone only sends instructions. No Ubuntu, no local storage. Each conversation binds its own environment, so topics never cross. Two ways in: an HTTP service (deploy bundle below) or SSH straight into a Linux box (nothing to install).
The connection details for \"%1$s\" will be removed. Files on that machine are untouched.
\"%1$s\" is in use by this conversation. After deleting, it falls back to the local workspace.
Connected (root path silent, exec channel works).
Cannot reach it: check the address, the token, and whether the service is still running.

SSH needs nothing installed on the server: commands go through exec channels, files through SFTP, with exactly the same capabilities as the HTTP service. On first connect a small helper script is placed in ~/.dsha/ (deleting it does no harm). Host keys are not pinned (a rebuilt server will not lock you out); verify the fingerprint after testing the connection.
Both come from whoever deployed it. Use the root address, without /exec.
Here is a ~30 KB deployment bundle. Send it to any AI that can operate a server, ask it to deploy per the instructions, and it will hand back an address and a token.
1. Tap “Copy deploy text” and paste it to any AI that can operate a server. 2. Ask it to deploy publicly and return an address and token. 3. Paste them above.
Copied. Paste it to any AI that can operate a server.
Failed to read the deploy bundle
No app can open zip files. Install a file manager first.
Saved to %1$s — file managers will open right in this folder
Saved to %1$s (app-private; grant \"All files access\" to move it to Download/DSHA)
The token equals shell access on that machine. Do not post it publicly. The service is not sandboxed — run it as a regular user.
Reads, writes and commands in this chat all happen on that machine.
For when you neither want a container nor want the agent touching phone storage. Once bound, this chat\'s file and shell tools all move to the cloud.
Reads run freely; writes, commands and screen actions ask first
Files and commands (including root) run freely; third-party tools and screen still ask
Never ask again, including deletes, root and third-party calls
Every tool call will run immediately without confirmation — including deleting files, running commands as root and operating the screen. Only enable this when you trust the task and the environment.
This chat has no cloud environment bound yet.
Ring a system notification at the set time. You can also just tell the AI: "remind me to drink water at 8 every morning".
Notifies you when the time comes

With root, input / uiautomator / screencap can be run through su without the accessibility service. When both channels work, accessibility is preferred (node fingerprints make mis-taps far less likely); root is the fallback. The grant dialog comes from Magisk / KernelSU — this app never escalates by itself.
Enable it in system settings; reads real view nodes
Grant su once, survives a reboot
Foreground app only. Passwords and payment pages are never read. Every action shows a banner at the top. You can stop it from the chat page at any time.
Tell the AI who you are; applied to every chat
Describe who you are, how you want to be addressed, and what kind of answers you prefer. It goes at the very top of the system prompt and applies to every conversation.
e.g. I am Zhang, working on pentesting and C++. Be direct, skip the pleasantries, prefer code over prose.
Summarize old turns once the threshold is reached
Pull relevant snippets from other chats as background
Type below, then press enter or the arrow. Select several images at once or attach files; hold the empty composer to talk.
Add an endpoint in Settings — official, a relay, or something local — and the model list is pulled straight from it. Tap the top of the chat to switch; context length follows the model.
Five thinking levels. Hard problems to the right, small talk to the left, turn it off when you don\'t need it.

The ring on the left shows context used. Old turns get summarized automatically once you reach the threshold, or tap the ring to compact now. The threshold scales with the window — a 32K model compacts at 70%, a 1M model waits until 90%.
Turn on Agent and it can read files, run commands and drive the screen. Every action passes through your approval level first.

A preset is a named system prompt — write it once, use it anywhere. The persona covers \"who I am\", the preset covers \"how to answer\", and the per-chat note covers \"what this one is about\". Presets can be imported straight from a document: plain text, Markdown or JSON all work.
The workspace is where the AI actually works: reading files, editing code, running scripts. It edits real files, not a block of text in the chat.
Borrow a machine when yours is too small
A cloud workspace is a remote Linux box: install packages, compile, run long jobs. Enter the address and token once, then bind it to any conversation.
A real Linux: bash + apt + gcc, runs any terminal command. ~30 MB download, ~300 MB on disk.
Deletes the whole Ubuntu root filesystem, including packages and files you created inside it. Workspace files are untouched.
CPython inside the Ubuntu environment. Once it is there the AI can run scripts directly, instead of rewriting every one of them as a shell command.
No bookmarks yet. Long-press a file or folder and choose Bookmark.
Copy / move lands in the other pane: %1$s
“%1$s” will be deleted permanently. There is no recycle bin.
The preview server listens on 127.0.0.1 only; other devices on the same Wi-Fi cannot see it.
File is larger than %1$s; only the beginning is shown.
Standard MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0 / Streamable HTTP): the URL must be the endpoint, usually https://host/mcp; put tokens as Authorization: Bearer xxx.
Cannot read this folder. Grant “All files access” in Settings → Permissions.
Too large; up to %1$s per file.
The server is an older build without /fs/upload. Redeploy it from the Cloud Workspace page with the latest bundle (v3 and later).
Type a command and send. Each tab is an isolated session: cwd, history and shell are its own.
MCP: give the model external tools
Connect a server and its tools show up in the model\'s hands. Standard MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0 / Streamable HTTP) and local stdio are supported.

Compression fires when either threshold is met: usage reaches the ratio above, or you have sent this many messages since the last summary. The ratio and the count are base values — the real trigger moves later as the window grows (32K at 70%, 1M at 90%). Tap the number to type an exact value; the slider only offers common steps. The summary keeps its fixed four sections — this page only controls *when* it happens.

The three switches above decide *when* compaction happens. The ratio and the message count are base values — the real trigger moves later as the window grows: a 32K model compacts at 70%, a 1M model waits until 90%. After a compaction the usage drops below the trigger, so it never re-compacts the same turns round after round.
(Nobody is talking right now. You may speak up on your own: one or two sentences that pick up what was being discussed. Do not mention this note, and do not ask "are you still there".)
Type into the box below.\nSay what you want — no manual needed.
Menu at top left: history and search.\nThe chip by the composer: switch model, toggle thinking.\nThe ⋯ at top right: files, terminal, settings.
Swipe left or right, one card at a time
Organize this project and create a report
Chance is per hour; it only speaks after the configured idle time.
A skill is text appended to the system prompt while enabled; turning it off removes it entirely.
When on, this server\'s tools appear in the model\'s tool list; turning it off removes them and keeps the config.
stdio starts a local process. Android has no npx / uvx; install the runtime inside the built-in Ubuntu or Termux and use its absolute path.
Accepts an mcpServers config or a single { command / url } object. Everything stays editable after import.
No server found in the JSON
Reads the accessibility tree: text, buttons, precise targets. Works for most apps.
Looks at a screenshot and taps coordinates. For games and canvas UIs that expose no controls. Screenshots stay in memory.

Once picked, the AI only gets the tools for that mode — it cannot switch to the other one on its own. Screenshot mode sends the current frame with every observation, along with resolution and scale, for UE/Unity style scenes.
Removes this profile’s address, key and model list. Conversations are untouched.
Delete "%1$s"? Files inside will be removed permanently.
No internal workspace yet. Create one from the workspace chip in chat.
Every command the AI ran is logged here, read-only. Open another tab to type your own.
Post a notification when the time comes.
Run a shell command at the scheduled time; output goes into the notification. Works with the app in the background.
Only notify when the command fails. Good for daily backups and cleanups.
The system voice always works; the official voice sounds better but needs an official key; a custom API can point at any OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint.
A base URL or the full endpoint both work; /audio/speech is appended when missing.
One Key: Value per line. For gateways that need custom auth headers.
Speak every finished reply automatically. Off by default.
An OpenAI-compatible /images/generations endpoint. Once configured, the AI can draw.
When unset, the drawing tool is not offered to the model, so it asks you to configure it instead of retrying failures. Once configured, just describe the picture in chat (Agent mode on).
Fill in endpoint, key and model, and the AI can draw
No models yet. Tap "Fetch models" below, or enter one manually.
Fetch from the server, or enter a model id manually
Auto means the AI decides the shape from what you asked for (portrait, landscape, square) — not always a square. A size pinned here is only a fallback; an explicit request in the chat wins.
WIDTHxHEIGHT, e.g. 1024x1024. Leave empty for auto.
%1$d items will be deleted permanently. Continue?
Swipe a row right to select
Any endpoint URL, local or remote; HTTPS works too.
(%d older attachment(s) omitted here to save context; ask the user to re-upload if needed)
Appended to the end of the compaction prompt, highest priority. Put what must never be lost here.
e.g. copy every identifier, path and command verbatim; never round numbers or versions.
Stopped (interrupted by user; the tool did not finish)
Test timed out: no response within 25s. The endpoint may be routing /models to a backend that never answers.
Chooses which models are listed in the chat\'s model switcher. It doesn\'t change the current model above.
Add an API key first, then test.
